question: OWN-1: can an unprivileged, non-entitled Loom find and stop every process forked by a managed run (including unmarked setsid + double-fork escapes reparented to launchd) without signaling outside processes?

verified.claim: A non-AppKit LSBackgroundOnly helper app launched through LaunchServices (open -n, NSWorkspace createsNewApplicationInstance) starts as the sole member of a fresh resource coalition, distinct from the caller's.
verified.result: Caller (terminal) coalition 43043; helpers 57123, 57125, 57127, 57158, 57170 and 9 parallel NSWorkspace launches all distinct; each helper sole member at start.

verified.claim: An unmarked Apple platform binary (/bin/sleep) started via setsid + double fork stays in the helper coalition after reparenting to launchd and after the helper exits; launchd does not kill it.
verified.result: Escapee pid 97491 ppid=1 sid=self res=57123 remained sole member after helper exit.

verified.claim: Work handed to launchd or LaunchServices leaves the run coalition.
verified.result: Nested open -n from inside a run -> new coalition 57129; launchctl submit job -> new coalition 57131 (launchctl remove killed it). Such work is outside the run scope by construction, like an app opened from a terminal.

verified.claim: Loom cannot create a coalition or spawn into one itself.
verified.result: coalition(CREATE) -> EPERM locally. XNU sys_coalition.c and kern_exec.c gate create/spawn-into-coalition on a privileged coalition or com.apple.private.coalition-spawn (explorer source read, xnu-12377.1.9).

verified.claim: Per-requester Apple XPC instances join the run coalition when a run process requests them, and launchd removes them when their client is gone.
verified.result: metalprobe in run 57158 caused MTLCompilerService (ppid=1) to join; after the client was killed the coalition was empty within 5 s without any signal to the service. App coalitions of Chrome/Slack/Obsidian/Terminal also contain such instances (SetStoreUpdateService etc.), which is why Loom's own app coalition is not a clean ownership boundary.

verified.claim: PROC_PIDUNIQIDENTIFIERINFO.p_orig_ppidversion separates launchd-spawned members from forked work even after reparent + exec; p_puniqueid does not.
verified.result: launchd idversion 760. Helper, apps and all XPC instances: orig_ppidversion=760. Escapee that exec'd after reparent: puniqueid=1 (misleading) but orig_ppidversion=1181289. XNU kern_fork.c:982-998 sets orig ppid/version at fork and copies them across exec; proc_reparentlocked only changes p_pptr/p_ppid; pinsertchild rewrites p_puniqueid on exec.

verified.claim: Freeze-then-kill loop over forked coalition members converges against an adversarial escapee and never signals outside processes.
verified.result: Churner ignoring SIGHUP/SIGTERM and re-forking with setsid every ~0.5 ms created 1729 /bin/sleep members in 3 s plus a Metal client. Drain (SIGSTOP all forked members, re-verify pid version + coalition, then SIGKILL; never signal launchd-spawned members) left only the helper; MTLCompilerService was removed by launchd; after the helper stopped the coalition was empty. Control /bin/sleep in another coalition stayed alive. Final check: 0 sleepers, 0 churners.

Helper (C, no frameworks) footprint 1088 KB, RSS ~1.5 MB. Ready (own handshake proxy) 33-75 ms for 8 parallel NSWorkspace launches. NSWorkspace completion handler waits ~30 s because the helper does not check in with LaunchServices; readiness must come from Loom's own socket handshake, not that callback.

unverified: PTY slave passed over SCM_RIGHTS to the helper with TIOCSCTTY and real Claude/Codex TUIs inside a run scope
Behavior under sudo/setuid inside a scope (members with another uid cannot be signaled; must be an honest failure)
Long-running/idle XPC instances that launchd keeps alive after their client is gone (must surface as unverified stop, not success)
Crash/Force-Quit behavior of helpers; recovery by stored coalition IDs within the same boot
Private proc_pidinfo flavors 17 and 20 on future macOS releases (fail closed on layout change, as today)
Codex shared app-server: command escapes cannot be attributed to one Codex session while several share the server
